headline: Tax-season strength drives a beat and a raised outlook
summary_short: Intuit's fiscal Q3 revenue rose 10% y/y to $8.56B and diluted EPS climbed 11% to $11.09, as the company raised full-year revenue guidance to $21.34-21.37B and announced a 17% workforce reduction with $300-340M in restructuring charges.
summary_long: Revenue rose 10% y/y to $8.56B, driven by Global Business Solutions Online Ecosystem revenue +19% (QuickBooks Online Accounting +22%) and Consumer revenue +8% (TurboTax +7%, Credit Karma +15%). GAAP operating income grew 8% to $4.02B; GAAP diluted EPS was $11.09 (+11%), non-GAAP diluted EPS $12.80 (+10%). Intuit raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $21.34-21.37B and non-GAAP EPS guidance to $23.80-23.85. It repurchased $1.6B of stock, added an $8B buyback authorization, and raised its quarterly dividend 15% to $1.20/share. The company also announced a 17% workforce reduction with $300-340M in restructuring charges, mostly in fiscal Q4. Cash and investments were $6.8B against $6.2B debt.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by Online Ecosystem revenue +19% (QuickBooks Online Accounting +22%, Online Services +15%) and Consumer revenue +8% (TurboTax +7%, Credit Karma +15% on personal loans, auto insurance, home loans).
Not itemized beyond overall revenue growth; operating income (+8%) grew slower than revenue (+10%) as selling/marketing (+11%) and R&D (+19%) both rose, implying modest margin compression.
Tracks operating-income growth plus a lower diluted share count (276M vs 282M y/y, aided by $1.6B of buybacks this quarter) and higher interest/other income ($97M vs $32M y/y).

Management attributes the quarter to its 'AI-driven expert platform strategy' scaling growth engines in assisted tax, money, and mid-market business (growing over 30%); CFO cites 'disciplined capital allocation' behind the raised guidance.
